name: Zopiclone

lead: Zopiclone is a prescription sleeping pill used in Europe, Canada and elsewhere for short-term severe insomnia.
It has not been tested for appearance; forum mentions are about sleep.

paras: It enhances GABA-A receptor signalling at the benzodiazepine site, causing sedation.
Reported effects include drowsiness, bitter taste, amnesia, behavioural changes, tolerance and dependence; treatment is usually limited to about four weeks.

lead: Zopiclone is a prescription nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic of the cyclopyrrolone class used for short-term treatment of severe insomnia in adults. It acts at the benzodiazepine site of the GABA-A receptor.[1]

Grokipedia reports it was first patented in 1972 and marketed from 1986 by Rhone-Poulenc under names such as Imovane and Zimovane; it is not approved in the United States, where its (S)-enantiomer eszopiclone is used.[1]
It has no appearance indication. On looksmax.org it appears in occasional threads about sleep aids.[2]
infobox: Prescription-only; not approved in the US[1]

paras: Zopiclone is indicated for short-term treatment of severe insomnia causing distress or functional impairment, with treatment typically limited to about four weeks.[1]

Common effects include a bitter taste, drowsiness, dizziness and dry mouth; more serious risks include anterograde amnesia, behavioural changes such as hallucinations or agitation, tolerance, dependence and rebound insomnia on stopping.[1] A review of case reports and epidemiological data examined abuse and dependence potential for zolpidem and zopiclone.[3]

A randomised trial compared cognitive behavioural therapy with zopiclone for chronic insomnia in older adults.[4] A BMJ meta-analysis examined short-term sedative hypnotics including zopiclone in older people.[5] An observational study examined road-traffic accidents and benzodiazepine use.[6] A Lancet network meta-analysis covers hypnotics for insomnia.[7] A registered trial compared eszopiclone with zopiclone.[8] No studies of appearance outcomes were found.

lore.intro: Zopiclone is mentioned in occasional looksmax.org threads on sleep aids and long-term use.[2]

claims.claim: Sleeping pills like zopiclone improve sleep but harm sleep quality over time.

timeline.event: Rhone-Poulenc introduces zopiclone to the market.[1]
